title.value: Using Confounded Data in Latent Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
title.justification: The paper is centered on the use of confounded data within reinforcement learning, focusing on improving sample-efficiency in learning models.
title.quote: Abstract In the presence of confounding, naively using off-the-shelf offline reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms leads to sub-optimal behaviour. In this work, we propose a safe method to exploit confounded offline data in model-based RL.

extractions.description: This paper addresses the challenge of using confounded data in model-based reinforcement learning. It proposes a method to improve the sample-efficiency of an RL agent by correctly utilizing confounded offline data along with online data. The method incorporates causal inference via do-calculus to adjust for confounding effects, demonstrating improvements in learning efficiency over traditional methods that do not account for confounding.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses primarily on methodological advancements in reinforcement learning and causal inference, with no direct emphasis on climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Broader Impact Statement Confounding is a prevalent issue in human-generated data, and can be an important source of bias in the design of decision policies, if not dealt with properly.

primary_category.quote: This paper makes a humble step towards more robustness and fairness in AI-based decision systems, by combining causality and statistical learning to address the confounding problem in reinforcement learning from offline data.
